newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japan needs decisive structural reforms -IMF.
newsitem.headline: Japan needs decisive structural reforms -IMF.

text.p: Japan needs to initiate decisive structural reforms to foster stronger growth in the medium-term, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in a paper due to be presented to Asia Pacific finance ministers at the weekend.
Japan's recovery has become more broad-based, reflecting accomodative monetary policies, the correction of the overvaluation of the yen, and temporary fiscal stimulus, it said.
"While monetary policy needs to continue to support the recovery, the large fiscal deficit will need to be corrected at a sustained pace envisaged in the proposed FY 1997 budget.

"If, however, economic activity proves significantly weaker than expected, the speed of fiscal consolidation may have to be reviewed. Decisive structural reforms are needed to foster stronger growth in the medium-term," the IMF said.

The paper, a copy of which was acquired by Reuters on Thursday, is to be presented to finance ministers of 18 member economies of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum when they meet on Saturday in Cebu in the central Philippines.
In Japan, despite the pessimism recently apparent in equity markets, economic indicators generally point to continuing recovery at a moderate underlying pace, the IMF said.

Growth was strong in the fourth quarter after modest gains in the third. In 1997, the contractionary effects of tax increases and lower public investment should be offset by a recovery in labour income and rising net exports. the IMF said.
"There is upside potential for growth to exceed the forecast, but there are also significant downside risks which are amplified by weaknesses in the financial sector," the paper said.
The APEC ministers' discussions include finding ways to ensure a freer flow of capital in the region.
Among those attending the meeting are Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
